sentence: This project builds computational methods that track how pieces of DNA jump to other places in the genome in cancer.
This project tests whether a breast MRI method combined with near-infrared spectroscopic tomography can replace contrast injection.
This project tries to find out which genetic variants actually cause birth defects in patients with rare diseases.
This project builds probes that image and measure small molecules and neurotransmitters around single cells.
This project studies how a female-specific long noncoding RNA may raise the risk of autoimmune disease.
This project provides animal models of ocular diseases and imaging tools to study how those diseases work.
This project studies how cells of the human brain differ from person to person in the genes they use.
This project provides histology, microscopy and image analysis tools, including artificial intelligence methods, for studying ocular tissues.
This project studies how neuro-immune signaling in the amygdala helps acute pain become chronic pain.
This project studies how a single exposure to fentanyl harms the gut microbiome and brain function over time.
This project tests whether R-pyocins, which are antimicrobial proteins, can treat drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa wound infections.
This project studies how norepinephrine affects learning to link cues with rewards, which may relate to relapse in substance-use disorder.
This project builds a statistical method that combines genomic and transcriptomic data to find gene signatures for sorting cancer patients.
This project uses machine learning on medical record data to find Veterans who should be checked for undiagnosed axial spondyloarthritis.
This project uses CRISPR gene editing to try to treat heart attack, stroke, Marfan syndrome and inherited forms of heart failure.
This project studies how the structures of bryostatin and related natural and designed molecules affect their binding and biological activity.
This project manages imaging and radiation therapy in cancer trials so that results stay consistent across participating sites.
This project develops metal-based methods to label molecules with fluorine-18 for imaging.
